Assumption: documents are JSON bodies plus metadata, grouped in collections; large binaries would go via presigned upload URLs, not through this API.

```
GET|POST          /v1/collections
GET|PATCH|DELETE  /v1/collections/{id}
GET|POST          /v1/documents            ?collection_id=&limit=&cursor=
GET|PUT|PATCH|DELETE /v1/documents/{id}
GET               /v1/documents/{id}/revisions
GET               /v1/documents/{id}/revisions/{rev}
POST              /v1/documents/{id}/restore   {"revision": 7}
```

**Resources.** Documents are flat, not nested under collections: a document can move collections without its URL changing. IDs are opaque and prefixed (`doc_01J…`, UUIDv7): sortable, unguessable, type visible in logs. Writes use optimistic concurrency: `ETag` on GET, `If-Match` required on PUT/PATCH/DELETE (missing → 428, stale → 412), so there are no silent lost updates. PATCH is JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396). POST accepts `Idempotency-Key`, so retries are safe.

**Tenancy and auth.** Tenant comes from the credential, never from the URL or body. With no tenant ID in the path, a client cannot ask for another tenant's data by editing it. Bearer tokens only: short-lived JWTs for users (OIDC), hashed API keys for machines; both resolve to `tenant_id` plus scopes (`documents:read`, `documents:write`, `collections:admin`). A user in several tenants gets one token per tenant. Enforce isolation in the data layer (row-level security or tenant-prefixed keys), not only in handlers, because one forgotten `WHERE` must not leak. Another tenant's resource returns 404, not 403, so existence does not leak. Rate limits are per tenant: 429 + `Retry-After`.

**Pagination.** Cursor-based (keyset) on `(created_at, id)`:

```json
{"data": [...], "next_cursor": "b3BhcXVl", "has_more": true}
```

Offset pagination skips or duplicates rows under concurrent writes and gets slower with depth; keyset is stable and cost is flat at any depth. Cursor is opaque and bound to the filter and sort (mismatch → 400), so its encoding can change later. `limit` defaults to 50, max 200. No total count: expensive on large tenants.

**Versioning.** Major version in the path (`/v1`): visible, cacheable, trivially routable. Additive changes (new fields, new endpoints, new optional params) ship without a bump; clients must ignore unknown fields. Breaking changes → `/v2`, with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers on v1. Date-header versioning (Stripe-style) is finer-grained but needs a transformation layer per version; skip until v1 proves insufficient. Document revisions are separate: integer per document, immutable, restore creates a new revision.

**Errors.** RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/validation",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "validation_failed",
  "detail": "2 fields invalid",
  "request_id": "req_01J…",
  "errors": [{"field": "title", "code": "too_long", "message": "max 255 chars"}]
}
```

A standard format gives clients one parser. `code` is the stable machine contract; `title` and `detail` are for humans and may change. `request_id` (also sent as a header) ties support tickets to logs. Status mapping: 400 malformed, 401 no or invalid token, 403 scope missing, 404 absent or other tenant's, 409 conflict, 412 stale ETag, 422 validation, 429 rate limit.
